name: Block / Counter
summary: When somebody speeds the ball up at you from the kitchen line, you either block it soft so it drops at their feet, or counter it back harder than it came. Both start from the same ready position, and choosing between them in the tenth of a second you have is most of what a hands battle is.
whenToUse: A speed-up is coming at you at the kitchen line and there is no time to move.
Block when the ball is at or below your chest, or you are off balance.
Counter when the ball is above the net and arriving where you can get in front of it.
Counter when they have committed forward and there is space behind them.
howTo: Hold the paddle up in front of your chest, tip above the wrist, before anything happens.
Keep your hands in front of your body — a paddle beside your hip cannot do either shot.
To block: loosen the grip, angle the face slightly open, and let the ball die into their kitchen.
To counter: firm the grip at contact and punch through the ball, aiming at the near shoulder.
Do not swing back. There is no time, and the pace is already supplied.
Reset the paddle to the middle immediately, because the next ball is coming just as fast.
commonMistakes: Starting with the paddle down, which loses the exchange before it begins.
Swinging at a fast ball, which turns a routine block into a ball flying past the baseline.
Countering something at your ankles, where the only thing available was a block.
Blocking with a tight grip, so the ball rebounds up and gets put away.
Turning the shoulders to reach a body ball instead of taking it with a backhand in front.

drills.name: Speed-up and block
drills.description: Your partner dinks and randomly speeds one up at your body. You block everything back into their kitchen — no counters allowed. It trains the default so the counter becomes the decision.

drills.name: Chest high, counter
drills.description: Same drill, but your partner only speeds up balls that will arrive above net height. Every one of those gets countered at their near shoulder. Anything lower, you leave.

mistake.label: Swung at instead of absorbed: a ball that already had pace leaves the paddle with more and lands beyond the baseline.

rows.label: Ball height
rows.other: Above the height of the net.

rows.label: Grip
rows.other: Firm at contact — you are adding it.

rows.label: Where it goes
rows.self: Dies in the first few feet of their kitchen.
rows.other: At the near shoulder, flat and fast.

rows.label: What it buys
rows.other: The point, or a pop-up you can finish.

rows.label: If you get it wrong
rows.self: Slightly high, and they attack again.
rows.other: Long, or straight into the net.
